subject: BlueLoom post-call: context & unit-econ clarifications
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Priyanka Shah <priyanka@blueloom.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: BlueLoom post-call: context & unit-econ clarifications

Hi Priyanka — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can get a clean pricing sketch over to you:

Recap from our call:
- Product: dynamic recommendations + session summaries for BlueLoom storefronts
- Expected traffic: ~75k MAUs with peak bursts tied to campaigns
- Current rough volume estimate: 18–22M API requests / month (mostly inference calls)
- Current ask: firm up average prompt & completion token mix, and confirm how often you need longer context (32k/128k) vs 8k

Clarifying / ask items (if you can confirm in reply):
1) Avg prompt tokens per request (rough): we discussed 'short' prompts — is 90–130 tokens in line?
2) Avg completion tokens per request (rough): we heard approx 300–600 tokens — can you pick a single working average (helps pricing)
3) Context distribution: approx % of requests needing:
   - 8k context (baseline)
   - 32k context (long threads / transcript enrichment)
   - 128k context (rare analytic jobs)
4) Target unit-econ you want us to aim for: $/1M tokens or a monthly budget band — you mentioned wanting to stay < $X/1M in the call; want to confirm a numerical target (e.g., $15–25 / 1M tokens) or a monthly budget range (e.g., $10k–$30k)

What we can provide next once we have those numbers:
- A quick spreadsheet that models token mix, projected monthly token counts, and two pricing paths (hosted with usage pricing vs. Dedicated reserved commit)
- A recommendation on whether you should plan for 32k-enabled endpoints (and only route 12% of traffic there) vs. keeping everything on 8k with occasional fallbacks

Attachments: redwood-pricing-estimate-v2.pdf (sketch), sample usage template (CSV) attached for your convenience.

If easiest, reply inline to the 4 asks and I’ll turn this into a one-pager and a firm quote. I can also book a technical deep-dive with Dylan this week to go over the 32k/128k checklist.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
alex@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Priyanka Shah <priyanka@blueloom.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Goyal <samir.g@blueloom.com>, BlueLoom Procurement <procurement@blueloom.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BlueLoom post-call: context & unit-econ clarifications

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers below (inline):

> 1) Avg prompt tokens per request (rough): we discussed 'short' prompts — is 90–130 tokens in line?
Yes — 110 tokens is a good working average.

> 2) Avg completion tokens per request (rough): we heard approx 300–600 tokens — can you pick a single working average (helps pricing)
Working average ~420 tokens. Some responses are under 100, some very long (1000–1500) for summarization jobs, but 420 is a reasonable expectation.

> 3) Context distribution: approx % of requests needing: 8k / 32k / 128k
Our telemetry suggests:
- 8k: ~86% of calls (standard recs/small summaries)
- 32k: ~12% (session aggregation, long order histories)
- 128k: ~2% (full-session analytics / audit exports)

> 4) Target unit-econ you want us to aim for: $/1M tokens or a monthly budget band
We’re targeting an initial monthly budget of $12k–$28k while we validate early results. For unit-econ, finance would prefer to see options in the $12–20 / 1M tokens band; anything north of $25 / 1M will be hard to justify without committed discounts.

I attached an anonymized sample of recent queries (fields: request_id, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, timestamp). Let me know if you need the raw logs or a longer time window.

Thanks — Priyanka
Priyanka Shah
Head of ML Products, BlueLoom
priyanka@blueloom.com | +1 (212) 555-5687

[Attachment: anon-query-sample.csv (CSV, 1.2MB)]

Subject: Re: BlueLoom post-call: context & unit-econ clarifications

Thanks Priyanka & Alex — good detail. A couple internal notes for the thread (Lauren replying-all):

Alex: pricing guidance and next steps
- Unit-econ targets: aim to present two posture options:
  1) Hosted usage tier with volume discounts that targets ~$18 / 1M tokens for the blended mix (based on Priyanka's 110/420 avg and 18–22M requests/mo).
  2) Reserved/Dedicated offer: show committed throughput (e.g., 4–8 GPUs) with an effective blended rate closer to ~$10–13 / 1M tokens at higher commits and binning the 32k/128k usage to a separate pricing ladder.
- Note on context sizing: because 32k is only ~12% and 128k only ~2%, we recommend an approach where the majority of traffic stays on optimized 8k endpoints and only the heavy jobs route to provisioned 32k/128k nodes. This reduces cost and keeps latency predictable.
- SLA/compliance: BlueLoom flagged encryption-at-rest + audit logs — Dylan, please include the SOC2 evidence and the private-deploy checklist in the package we send.

Dylan: can you assemble a technical appendix that covers:
- Memory/KV cache impact for 32k vs 128k on batch sizing
- Expected latency delta and recommended qps throttles for long-context routes
- Ops checklist and estimated onboarding timeline (2–4 weeks for hosted, 6–10 weeks for private)

I’ll let Alex lead the commercial outreach; Dylan, can you aim to have the appendix + a first-pass committed pricing spreadsheet by Monday PDT? Alex — I’ll back any ask for a short-term pilot credit to help cover validation if they ask.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Director, Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0133
